chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khattab ibn Muhammad, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) met me on a road in Medina and said: 'Who is that? Is it Harith?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, I shall carry the sins of your foolish ones upon your knowledgeable ones.' Then he passed by. So I came to him and sought permission to enter. I entered and said: 'You met me and said, "I shall carry the sins of your foolish ones upon your knowledgeable ones," and a great matter entered my heart because of that.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. What prevents you, when word reaches you about a man among you that you dislike, and which causes us hurt, that you go to him, reproach him, correct him, and speak to him with eloquent words?'
I said to him (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, then they will not obey us and will not accept from us?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Flee from them and avoid their gatherings.'

key_terms.سُفَهَاءُكُمْ: Your foolish ones (those prone to error/ignorance)

ai.seo_question: How do scholars carry the sins of the general public according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith elucidates the Shia concept of 'Amr bil Ma'ruf wa Nahi anil Munkar' (Commanding Good and Forbidding Evil), establishing that scholars bear the burden of the community's errors if they neglect corrective action. The Imam outlines a graduated approach: first, direct and eloquent reproach; if that fails, social distancing (Hijr) to prevent the spread of corruption. This reflects the scholarly tradition where the 'Ulama' are seen as the guardians of the community's moral integrity, linking individual piety to collective responsibility.

en.hubeali: H 14617 – Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khataab Bin Muhammad, from Al-Haris Bin Al-Mugheira, who has narrated the following:

Abu Abdullahasws met me in a road of Al-Medina, so heasws said: ‘Who is that? Is it Haaris?’ I said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘But Iasws shall dump the sins of your foolish ones upon your knowledgeable ones’. Then heasws passed by. So I came up to himasws and sought permission to see himasws. I said, ‘Youasws met me and youasws said, ‘Iasws shall dump the sins of your foolish ones upon your knowledgeable ones’, and that was a great matter upon me’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. What prevented you when it reached you from the man among you what you dislike, as it enters hurtful feelings to us<sup>asws</sup>, (you should) go to him and reproach him, and correct it (his wrong doings), and speak to him in eloquent words?’
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, if he does not obey us and does not accept from us?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Flee from him, and avoid their gatherings’ (stop accompanying him).
